<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via idp_provisioned (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in actions; a string literal in applyUserManagerLink))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via idp_provisioned (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in actions; a string literal in applyUserManagerLink))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via idp_provisioned (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in actions; a string literal in applyUserManagerLink))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-import-users.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `866f210f821ba351173e709307ba23ac5f7ff840` — the merge of head `5787dda5126ee75af2bb2cef8ab2f1b5d3776d33` into base `bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 866f210f821ba351173e709307ba23ac5f7ff840 && git checkout 866f210f821ba351173e709307ba23ac5f7ff840
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262 5787dda5126ee75af2bb2cef8ab2f1b5d3776d33 && git checkout -B drift-repro bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262 && git merge --no-ff 5787dda5126ee75af2bb2cef8ab2f1b5d3776d33

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bc6b7ffd454ba9c2c420975c84a400779cb02262` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `fa70eaa067974408121386101990b9804fb5e08a`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T16:09Z · diff read against the merge's main parent `895783a1` (16 files, +302/−96, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jVPGBoi3MCGoKbW1Hv (area S1 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM

**Contract face:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with no narrowing arm, no `packages/spec/src` path and no governed text, so the record is owed at `TIER_DEFAULT`. The area's record is comment 6896964420 (PASS). This verdict is the ordinary ACCEPT read of the whole diff.

**What holds**

- **The rule matches the ruling.** Refusal 5 now needs both `source === 'idp_provisioned'` and a `sys_scim_subject` row. That is option A of ruling record 6895645364: "directory wins" applies only where a directory exists. Because `source` stays a conjunct, a SCIM-linked user with a local password (still `env_native`) keeps the answer it had. That case is pinned, and so is the fact that no SCIM read happens for it.
- **One predicate, not a copy.** `isHeldByScimDirectory` is lifted out of `judgeScimSsoAdoption`, and the adoption judgement's behaviour is unchanged. The endpoint imports it. The import's `manager_id` column reaches it through `applyUserManagerLink`, and a source pin checks that the import names neither the table nor the predicate.
- **Fails closed.** Only `isMissingTableError(e, 'sys_scim_subject')` reads as "not held". That passes `readObject`, as the callers gate requires, and follows the `scim-identity-source.ts` precedent. Any other read failure propagates and writes nothing, which is pinned. `sys_scim_subject` is a registered platform object, so an install without SCIM reaches the missing-table leg, not an unknown-object error.
- **Widening only.** The code, status and `details.reason` of the refusal are unchanged, and only the sentence changes. The self-assignment, cycle, depth and cross-organization refusals still apply to an SSO-only identity, which is pinned for self-assignment. Nothing accepted before is refused now. The Set Manager action's `visible` predicate drops to the standing platform-admin predicate. The endpoint still refuses a SCIM-held row and names the directory, so the button cannot write what the door refuses. The feature-gate matrix row is updated to match.
- **The text is true of the doors.** The lint remedy, the docblocks, the three docs pages and the changeset all say "a SCIM directory holds" and give the SSO-only path. The lint test asserts that the old `source 'idp_provisioned'` sentence is gone. The changeset patches all three published packages, and `Metadata-protocol: none` is right because no authorable key moves.
- **Tests.** Set and clear on a SCIM-held identity are both refused. Set and clear on an SSO-only identity both land. The missing-table and failed-read legs and the import rows (SCIM-held refused, SSO-only `linked`) are covered, and the demo-staff harness reads the subject table. I accept the 7 ablations as reported.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

1. The predicate's docblock says the vendor never deletes a `sys_scim_subject` row. So a person whose SCIM connection was later removed stays refused, and the message sends the admin to a directory that is gone. That is no regression, because before this PR every `idp_provisioned` row was refused. File it only if someone measures it.

**Gates:** at review time 58 success, 10 skipped, none red, so every check is green.
